title: Terminal header: in narrow columns the buttons fold into one menu, names give way in order, and the context warning becomes an icon
summary: Narrow terminal headers now fold park, pin, zoom and font size into one menu, hide branch then project name before cutting the terminal name, and show the context warning as a red icon; 1 review fix (clicks inside the menu flagged the terminal).
friction: GitHub Actions registered no checks on the pull request, so the reviewer ran the full gate locally (about 10 min per round); the maintainer confirmed there is no CI for now

The first session ended with three dev agents mid-work and nothing committed; resuming cost one restart of every gate, and the user then asked to run stories one at a time because three in parallel was too heavy for the machine
lessons_learned: On this machine run /dev-next stories one at a time: three parallel gates (vitest plus cargo builds) overload it

deferred.what: The new ⋯ menu in the terminal header opens inside the pane, and eagle tiles and split-pane leaves clip their content, so in a short or narrow pane the lower font-zoom presets and the left edge of items cannot be clicked
deferred.why: Needs a positioning decision (portal, or opening upward or leftward), not a few lines

deferred.what: The header give-way order uses fixed widths while branch and Samurai pills never shrink, so between 360 and 479 px a long terminal name is cut while the whole branch shows, and below about 200 px a Samurai terminal's pills spill over the ⋯ and close buttons
deferred.why: Needs a design decision (compact Samurai badge, or hiding by measured overflow)
